title: qos.t1 re-bless's documented cause ('element changed bundle 1 -> 0') explains only the first tick; the 301-tick shift embeds an undocumented resolve + re-trigger churn
evidence:
git diff b94d54f..f906725 -- goldens/qos.t1:
  -1200 ca44329e929c4dbb
  -1201 38379d4bc0f441d8
  ...
  +1200 6124c5b772c0aa7b
  (all 301 ticks 1200-1500 rewritten; ticks 1-1199 byte-identical)
core/serialize.odin w_crises_section (the only persistent crisis bytes in the T1 hash):
  w_u32(w, ac.bundle)
  w_u32(w, ac.pipe)
  w_u16(w, ac.class)
  w_i32(w, ac.multiplier)
  w_u64(w, ac.triggered_tick)
app/render/crisis.odin (the only crisis fields that render):
  title = fmt.aprintf("!!  %s: %s ACTIVE — bundle %d (pipe %d)",
      arch, sp_name, ac.bundle, ac.pipe, allocator = context.temp_allocator)
harness/goldens.odin compare_images (zero tolerance):
  if pa[i] != pb[i] {
      mismatched += 1
CI run 31689620500 at f906725:
  PASS qos                  ticks=1500
  harness: 15 demo(s) green
core/crisis.odin CRISIS_RESOLVE_MARGIN comment:
  the golden discipline pins: a persistent flaw emits ONE trigger per activation [E13]
detail: T2@65s still renders 'bundle 1 (pipe 1)' (zero-tolerance compare, CI PASS) yet all 301 hashes differ: the persistent row's bundle/pipe cannot differ, so triggered_tick changed — bundle-0 trigger @1200, resolve, bundle-1 re-trigger. That cycle is documented nowhere; the 'ONE trigger' pin silently broke.
recommended_fix: Document the bundle-0 trigger → resolve → bundle-1 re-trigger sequence in the spec/commit and pin the re-trigger tick in a test; or require the (a) candidate to persist >1 tick so the transient bundle-0 row never fires.
